name: Red-shouldered Blackbird
rangeDescription: Marshes of western and central cuba and isla de la juventud (isle of pines)
description: A mostly black inhabitant of swamps and marshes. The male has a telltale orange-red shoulder patch with pale yellow trim, which the female lacks.

name: Annam Prinia
rangeDescription: Vietnam (langbian plateau)
description: A dull and poorly marked prinia with a strong bill and a long, graduated tail. Light brown above with faint dark streaking.

name: Rufous-throated Dipper
rangeDescription: Andes of southern bolivia (chuquisaca and tarija) and northwestern argentina (southward to catamarca and tucumán)
description: Dipper endemic to fast-moving streams in semi-humid montane forest with alders in Southern Bolivia and Northeast Argentina. The only dipper in its range.

name: Lilian's Lovebird
rangeDescription: Southern tanzania to malawi, zambia, zimbabwe, and mozambique
description: A gregarious small green parrot with a red bill, white eye-ring and orange-red face. Immature has a duller bill and eye-ring.

name: Flores Hawk-Eagle
rangeDescription: Lombok to alor (lesser sundas)
description: A large eagle with a bright white head and underside and a chocolate-brown back and uppertail. In flight, appears entirely white except for bold dark bars and tips on outer wings and tail.

name: Roll's Partridge
rangeDescription: Northwestern sumatra (batak highlands)
description: Restricted to montane and foothill broadleaf forests between 500 and 2000 meters in the Batak Highlands of northern Sumatra. Forages in dense vegetation on the forest floor, often pairs, but also singly and in small groups.

name: Orange-breasted Falcon
rangeDescription: Locally from southern mexico to northern argentina and brazil
description: Fairly large falcon; rare and local around clearings within large tracts of mature forest from southern Mexico to extreme northern Argentina. Very similar to much more common Bat Falcon.

name: Ancash Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Western andes of peru (southern cajamarca to ancash)
description: Small tapaculo found only at very high elevations in the western Andes of northern Peru. Plumage is gray with brown rear parts and dark barring on belly and tail.

name: Sharp-tailed Tyrant
rangeDescription: Eastern bolivia to south-central brazil, eastern paraguay, and northeastern argentina
description: A handsome tiny flycatcher with a long spiky tail. Note the conspicuous broad white eyebrow and white chin.

name: Hooded Monarch
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed lowland forest of new guinea
description: A medium-sized bird of lowland and foothill forest interior. Black upperparts and chest, white belly, grayish bill, fairly long tail and the hint of a bushy crest.

name: Purple Cochoa
rangeDescription: Montane forest of himalayas from northern india (uttarakhand) eastward to western arunachal pradesh and southern assam hills, eastern myanmar, south-central china (southern sichuan and yunnan), northwestern thailand, northern laos, and northern vietnam (northern tonkin)
description: An extremely shy and retiring bird, usually sluggish and difficult to see in well-shaded forests; coloration is unlike that of any typical thrush. At a distance, seems entirely dark with a soft purple crown and tail; up close, black face and wingtips are visible.

name: Munchique Wood-Wren
rangeDescription: Western andes of colombia
description: A small, stub-tailed wren endemic to Colombia’s western Andes. It has a long, white eyebrow and a streaky face.

name: New Ireland Dwarf-Kingfisher
rangeDescription: New hanover, new ireland, and lihir islands (eastern bismarck archipelago)
description: A small blue-and-orange kingfisher with an entirely black bill, ginger underparts, a white throat, and blue upperparts with a bright white neck spot. Found in dense mature forest habitats, often near streams and pools.

name: Blue Eared-Pheasant
rangeDescription: Montane forest of north-central china
description: A large gray terrestrial bird with an elegantly frilly tail. Bright red face and upswept white facial plumes (“ears”) are unique in its range.

name: Mamberamo Sunbird
rangeDescription: Northwestern new guinea and sepik ramu
description: Tiny and active sunbird of northern New Guinea. Male is dark gray-brown above, with an iridescent blue-black throat and black belly; small orange shoulder “spur” sometimes visible.

name: Buru Mountain-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Montane forest of buru (southern moluccas)
description: A large pigeon confined to Buru. Shows a pale gray crown and nape, slate-gray upperparts, and a cream throat and breast becoming salmon-pink on the belly.

name: Orinoco Piculet
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia, adjacent southern venezuela (southern amazonas), and northwestern brazil
description: This scarce piculet is known only from a few locations in the humid lowlands of eastern Colombia, southern Venezuela, and northwestern Brazil. Its underparts are entirely barred, but upperparts are plain, lacking the barring shown by the otherwise very similar Lafresnaye’s Piculet.

name: Mangrove Fantail
rangeDescription: Southeastern new guinea (trans-fly lowlands) and northern australia
description: Small pale gray flycatcher, exclusively coastal and usually observed in or very close to mangroves. Pale gray head and back, white throat and chin, pale wingbars, and a very thin gray chest band.

name: Golden-crowned Emerald
rangeDescription: Western mexico (southern sinaloa to durango, guerrero, and oaxaca)
description: Very small, fork-tailed hummingbird endemic to western Mexico. Favors scrubby woodland, forest edge, and flower banks; mainly in drier habitats.

name: Surf Scoter
rangeDescription: Breeds northern north america; winters to baja california and southern usa
description: Large, dark sea duck. Breeding males have a colorful bill and white patches on the nape and forehead.
